title: create() + Zod Validation
description: Safely accept user input, validate payloads with Zod schemas, and persist single and batch records with create() and createMany().
completionLearnings: Mastered single inserts (create) and batched high-throughput inserts (createMany with skipDuplicates: true)
Defined runtime validation contracts with Zod schemas before data ever touches the database
Inferred TypeScript types directly from Zod schemas with z.infer<typeof Schema>

concepts.title: Inserting Data (create(), createMany())
concepts.shortDescription: Persist records safely into the database with single and batch inserts.

theory.summary: prisma.model.create({ data: { ... } }) creates a single record and returns the newly inserted object with auto-generated IDs and timestamps. createMany({ data: [...], skipDuplicates: true }) inserts multiple rows in a single batch INSERT statement.

targetHero.explanation: Single record creation returning the persisted user object.

explanation: Single write (create): Performs INSERT INTO ... RETURNING *. Returns the fully populated entity.
Batch write (createMany): Performs a multi-row INSERT INTO ... VALUES (...), (...). Extremely fast for migrations and bulk CSV imports.
theory.keyTakeaway: Use createMany for high-throughput imports and create when you need the returned inserted object.

mcqs.question: Why does "prisma.model.createMany" not return the full array of created objects in standard PostgreSQL?
options: Because Prisma forbids reading data during writes
Because createMany optimizes for batch speed, returning { count: N } rather than hydrating entire object graphs
Because SQL does not support INSERT statements
Because TypeScript arrays cannot hold more than 10 items
mcqs.explanation: createMany returns a count object { count: number } for peak performance.

concepts.title: Validating Input Payloads with Zod
concepts.shortDescription: Never trust user input. Validate runtime payloads with Zod before writing to DB.

theory.summary: ORMs guarantee database schema types, but they do NOT validate runtime user input (e.g. valid emails, password lengths, or positive quantities). Zod validates payloads at the HTTP layer, ensuring only clean data reaches Prisma.

targetHero.explanation: Zod parses input at the HTTP boundary, inferring the TypeScript contract.

explanation: Schema.parse(rawBody): Throws a ZodError if any field fails validation, returning field-level issue details.
Type Safety: z.infer<typeof Schema> generates the exact TypeScript interface automatically.
theory.keyTakeaway: Always parse API inputs with Zod before calling prisma.model.create.

mcqs.question: What is the role of Zod when paired with Prisma in a web application?
options: Zod connects to the PostgreSQL database
Zod validates incoming client request bodies at runtime before database operations occur
mcqs.explanation: Zod guards the API boundary by rejecting malformed payloads before Prisma queries run.
